newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE OIL FUTURES TO STAY BULLISH, SUPPORTED.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE OIL FUTURES TO STAY BULLISH, SUPPORTED.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil prices are expected to continue to firm with the market generally bullish, good support in place and few bear flags being waved, analysts said.

Brent price action charted another fairly bullish day, but despite having broken through stiff resistance around $18.85 and then pushing through the psychological $19 barrier, the rally stalled at $19.15 and the market eventually settled back below $19, although at $18.99 only just.

The trading action continued a short-term trend of higher highs and higher lows stemming from last Friday's dip to $18.28. This pattern is usually deemed bullish and is also coupled with a pennant or flag formation on the spot month chart which may signal the resumption of the market's recent uptrend, analysts said.

The market also continued to hold above parallel trendline support drawn from the low of last Friday at the same angle as the bullish trend from July 21 to August 7 which continues to point the market higher.

"The market looked oversold on Monday and Tuesday. I was looking for some support in the absence of any major news in the market. This we saw (on Wednesday) with the market holding quite stable to close 10 cents up from Friday," said Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore.
"Brent looks technically bullish although I am more bullish WTI where there is more evidence of strong local demand," he added
Fibonacci resistance comes in initially around $19.20 today then there is some trendline resistance around $19.27.

Fourteen-day RSIs stand in neutral territory and there is little sign of a bearish convergence on the 10 and 20 moving average lines. Slow stochastics lines on the September chart are on the point of crossing but at this lower level are likely to point the market higher again.
Analysts said the September gas oil contract was now starting to look slightly bullish after the recent five trading day bearish trend.
"After holding the 50 percent retracement level on Monday and recovering it looks more positive," James said.
"I would become very bullish if we could see the trading gap $171 to $172 filled and break and close above $172," he added.
